title: Civil War
text: “W-what… N-n-no way… Could Fleon-chan have been… k-killed by the Crimson Swine…?”

“Yuki-chan comes from a good bloodline, right? Yet she’s turning into a Queen as if it were the most natural thing in the world. What’s the difference between her and that Fleon girl? If Fleon-chan grows up and takes on the form of an angel, who stands to lose the most?”
My breathing is getting labored from lack of oxygen. It feels as if everything is going dark before my eyes… a sense of despair is squeezing my chest.
What did you say? So does that mean I’ve been living my life blissfully unaware, without giving it a second thought, even though Fleon-chan was killed by the Crimson Swine by some means or another?
I picture the harrowing scene of Fleon-chan’s final moments. The Crimson Swine is laughing as he stomps on the hand Fleon-chan is reaching out, writhing in agony from poison!

“It’s the same with the King. As a father, he cherishes his son and daughter, but doesn’t he care more for the younger child? I have a younger brother, so I understand. As the older sibling, you end up with mixed feelings. Well, it might just be a coincidence that’s a bit too convenient, though.”
“No way…”

“Motoyasu, calm down. It might already be a thing of the past for you. But if you can come to realize this, you’ll be able to take a step forward. There are all sorts of questions surrounding that princess. It’s just a guess, but I think there’s a high probability it’s true.”
“That Crimson Swine! I’ll never forgive him!”
I feel like running out right this very moment to avenge Fleon-chan. But my reason stops me. If I were to kill the Crimson Swine now, all my hard work up to this point would be for nothing.

Still, my anger won’t subside. I want to sever all four of his limbs with this spear, keep him alive just long enough to apply healing spells as needed, turn him into a Daruma doll, and then kill him.
“Motoyasu, calm down!”
“Ugh… I get it!”

Hearing my Father’s words, I regained my composure. But the deep, dark hatred I feel toward the Crimson Swine won’t go away. If that bastard hadn’t meddled, maybe back then I could have reconciled with my Father without having to break the Spirit Tortoise’s seal! It’s impossible now, but I will—I absolutely, positively… make that bastard pay with his blood.
“For now, the problem is that Bitch of a princess. She’s with Itsuki right now, isn’t she? I’m starting to think this might actually be pretty dangerous.”
“She wasn’t with him the last time I saw him. When I was there, she was always in the same party as him.”
“Huh? My older sister was at the castle, though. She gave me her usual snide remarks.”
“Huh?”
“Huh?”
We were all left scratching our heads. That’s strange. Why isn’t Crimson Swine traveling with Itsuki?

“Ah… Maybe she knows she doesn’t get along with Itsuki’s personality, so she’s staying at the castle? You know, Itsuki seems to have a strong sense of justice, so maybe she doesn’t mesh well with that princess who’s always hatching schemes.”
“It’s not impossible. Crimson Swine doesn’t have a shred of a sense of justice, after all. If they spent a long time together, her true colors would probably show.”

That’s just like Crimson Swine. Come to think of it, even in the last loop, it felt like their relationship was rather distant. To begin with, I don’t think it’s easy to get in touch with Takt. After all, she didn’t act that way when she was with me in the first world.

The only conclusion we can draw from this is that she’s been getting by without relying on Takt by using me. Actually, just how close is the relationship between Crimson Swine and Takt, anyway? To be honest, I’m not really sure. However, if I recall vaguely, I seem to remember hearing that Crimson Swine lost her virginity in Faubrey in the past.
“I seem to recall hearing that Crimson Swine attended a school in Faubrey.”

The only conclusion I can draw from this is that Takt was that partner, and they got involved while they were in school, right? Given their ages, it’s not an impossible scenario. I led a somewhat wild life in high school myself, after all. Ugh… the trauma from that stain on my past—raping a pig.
“Yes, my older sister was enrolled at a school in Faubrey at one point. According to Mother, she wanted her to learn about the real world there… but Mother lamented that the outcome wasn’t good.”
“Well… how should I put it? Maybe it just didn’t work out because her heart is rotten…? She’s nothing like Melty-chan in personality.”

My finacée is making a rather awkward face. If she were anything like Crimson Swine, that would truly be a disgrace. Anyway, this lets us speculate on her connection to Takt as well. There must have been a difference between living a carefree, indulgent life in the castle and working as my companion.

Did the Crimson Swine even like Takt to begin with? He didn’t seem to fit in well among those pigs, so I suspect he wasn’t high on the priority list. And corruption… would it really be that easy to curry favor with Takt?
I can’t imagine the Crimson Swine would enjoy a place like that. After all, he’s a monster who enjoys watching others suffer.
“Well, wasn’t he easy to use before Motoyasu figured out the truth?”
“I’m sorry.”
“Don’t worry—you can’t say that for sure. If Motoyasu had pushed that Bitch princess away, he might’ve ended up fighting a powerful enemy before he was strong enough.”
That’s how my Father encouraged me. Ah… what a kind-hearted man he is. This Motoyasu here—the tears just keep flowing and won’t stop.
“Anyway, it looks like we can safely assume that Itsuki is acting independently of the king and that Bitch princess. He wasn’t there when we passed by, so I’m pretty sure of it.”
“That’s right.”
“In that case… it’s scary because we don’t know how this will play out. There’s still a chance—albeit a small one—that Itsuki might get killed by that guy, Takt.”
Both my father and my fiancée believe in my future. After all, we have to be wary of Takt, who possesses the ability to even steal the Four Holy Weapons.
“Hmm… I’m worried about Ren and Itsuki. If they were to die, all the hard work Motoyasu put into this loop would go down the drain.”
“Even if we have to loop again, I won’t give up!”
“I guess so… but I’d like you to think about my side of things, too. I’d hate for this loop to be treated as a sacrificial pawn and just swept under the rug.”
“So, should I capture Itsuki and Ren alive to protect them? Or—no, should I go kill Takt right now?”
“That’d be a tricky situation, wouldn’t it! If you kill him, it’ll lead to war, right?”
My father just scolded me. But they really are a troublesome bunch.
“Anyway, worrying won’t get us anywhere. Melty-chan, just hang in there a little longer, okay?”
“…Okay.”
When my fiancée lay down on the bed, Sakura-chan gently stroked her and began singing a lullaby. Keel and the other children soon began snoring as well.
“Let’s do our best so this won’t be in vain, Motoyasu-kun.”
“Yes, sir!”
I nodded energetically, and that was how we went to sleep that night.
Now, as for what happened to Melromarc after that…

Civilians across the country rallied in large numbers to oppose the government’s policies. Starting with Riyute Village—which had been saved by my Father—neighboring villages one after another praised the Shield Hero’s exploits and declared their conversion, accompanied by statements defying Melromarc’s policies.

Melromarc dismissed them, claiming they were “brainwashed by the Shield Demon.” The government deployed its military to carry out repeated “protective” roundups—which were really just forced detentions—and many were imprisoned.

The civilians reacted with fierce opposition to the government’s actions. As a result, they called themselves the Revolutionary Army, resolved to fight the Melromarc forces, and rose up. The Revolutionary Army, centered around civilians, gained more support than we could have imagined, and now Melromarc is scrambling to contain the situation.

Soon, as if to deliver the final blow, many civilians from neighboring countries joined the Revolutionary Army. It feels as though those who were saved by the “Saint of the Divine Bird”—now known as the Shield Hero—have joined their ranks.

Furthermore, even members of the Melromarc Army itself began defecting to the Revolutionary Army. They exposed the various misdeeds the nation had committed against the Shield Hero—misdeeds they knew firsthand. As a result, the Melromarc Army now finds itself with enemies within its own ranks.

Believing that capturing and executing the “Demon of the Shield” would quell the unrest, the Melromarc Army became desperate to capture my Father, while the revolutionary forces are raising their voices in support of him. Indeed, the times are calling for my Father, the Shield Hero, and the pent-up frustration of the oppressed people has finally erupted.

……Meanwhile, the voice of the sensible Queen—who had declared that the Shield Hero should be treated equally—is growing stronger, and the situation has reached a point where her return is being demanded. As for why the Queen’s return remains impossible, reports have leaked that the Three Heroes Church has consistently obstructed her duties and has repeatedly engaged in actions that could lead to war. Yes… the people have come to realize that the Three Heroes Church wants war more than it wants to quell the waves of calamity.

To make matters worse, there were the atrocities committed by Ren and Itsuki. They disrupted ecosystems across the land and resolved incidents only half-heartedly. Yes… Ren caused a plague to spread by leaving a dragon’s carcass unattended, and by exterminating monsters beyond what was necessary, he threw the ecosystem into chaos, leading to an increase in dangerous monsters—and reportedly, many villages suffered damage from them.

As for Itsuki, his half-hearted involvement in the revolution of a neighboring country failed to bring about a fundamental solution, leading to increased poverty and more people suffering under heavier taxes than before. There were also frequent incidents where supposedly virtuous lords were arrested and replaced by notorious ones.

Moreover, it seems testimonies are spreading that, although people were once saved by the Bow Hero, they were immediately exploited by other villains, and the outcome remained exactly the same. As a result of the actions of the Sword Hero and Bow Hero—which left the situation worse than before—the people’s trust began to shift toward the Shield Hero.

The people’s backlash turned against the church and, ultimately, the royal family. Rumors were spreading that the Shield Hero was protecting his Finacée—and that she was the very person who had dared to challenge the Wise King’s doctrine that the Shield Hero was evil, and was now in danger of being eliminated by the state.

Capitalizing on this were the moderates of Melromarc—members of the faction led by Éclair’s parents, who advocated for preferential treatment of Demi-Humans. Rumors that Éclair had been unjustly arrested, imprisoned, and tortured added fuel to the fire, and calls to “save her” spread rapidly.

With people determined to avoid being dragged into civil war, the exodus from the country showed no signs of stopping. Trash, Crimson Swine, and the Three Heroes Church—plagued by fierce internal strife and accusations of responsibility—seemed to be gradually being worn down.

And the final straw was a certain operation carried out by the Three Heroes Church… It seems that by the time the Church took the situation seriously and sprang into action, it was already too late. However, even then, they couldn’t bring themselves to back down, so they committed the most foolish act imaginable.

They massacred the villagers—who were increasingly spreading the teaching that they should worship the Shield Hero as an example. The Three Heroes Church impaled the bodies of those they had slaughtered and paraded them before the Revolutionary Army. Naturally, the result backfired.

The people’s anger reached a fever pitch, and the Revolutionary Army’s numbers continued to swell day by day. Eventually, the Revolutionary Army began marching toward Melromarc Castle in orderly ranks. Although civilians made up the bulk of their ranks, even the formidable Melromarc Army could not overcome the sheer force of numbers, and the Revolutionary Army is steadily closing in on the capital, advancing as if on a triumphant march. Now, access to Melromarc Castle and its outer gates is strictly restricted.
These were the events leading up to the wave.
And… the shift in the war’s tide has forced us to make many difficult choices.
